To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the application of high-resolution spectrum methods to power quality assessment can improve accuracy of measurement of power quality parameters, in particular the measurement of harmonic and interharmonics.

the use of the high-resolution spectrum estimation algorithms instead of FFT-based techniques improves the accuracy of the measurement of the spectral parameters of distorted power system waveforms, especially the estimation of the harmonic and interharmonics power quality indices.

The use of parametric methods instead of FFT-based techniques can improve accuracy of measurement of distorted waveforms, in particular the measurement of power quality indices (harmonic and interharmonic group/subgroup).
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the problem of power quality assessment based on parametric spectral estimation methods.
the application of parametric spectrum analysis methods in the field of power quality assessment.
the analysis of the accuracy of the power quality index estimation based on high-resolution spectral estimation methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
parametric methods are more accurate than FFT-based methods in estimation of spectral parameters.
parametric methods provide more accurate results than FFT-based techniques, but at a higher computational cost.
the use of parametric spectral analysis techniques is more accurate and more robust in comparison with the use of the FFT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

parametric spectral estimation methods provide a more accurate estimation of the spectral parameters, such as frequency, amplitude and phase of the spectral components, compared with Fourier-based algorithms.
parametric methods are better than FFT-based methods, but the difference is not so big.
the use of parametric spectral estimation methods can significantly improve the quality of measurement of spectral components in distorted waveforms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
parametric methods are more robust and accurate than FFT-based techniques.
parametric methods provide better estimation results than FFT-based methods.
the parametric methods can provide more accurate estimates of power quality indices than FFT-based techniques.
